title: Reducing quantum resources for ADAPT-VQE via plateau-operator elimination and correlated mean-field downfolding
authors: Phuoc Minh Vo, Thai Cong Ngoc Vu, Thien Ngoc Tran, Hoang Thanh Nguyen, Lan Nguyen Tran
abstract: Adaptive Derivative-Assembled Problem-Tailored variational quantum eigensolvers (ADAPT-VQE) represent one of the most promising approaches for quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices. However, their optimization is slow and may stall due to vanishing parameters and redundant operators in the ansatz. In this work, we propose a simple strategy of operator elimination that removes non-contributing operators from the pool once they are detected, enabling the optimization to continue progressing toward convergence. We examine two variants, with and without pool restoration after elimination, and find that the former converges more smoothly and faster than the latter and the standard ADAPT-VQE. To capture dynamical correlations between the active space and its environment, we combine ADAPT-VQE with our recently developed downfolding approach, the one-body downfolding framework (OBDF). In OBDF, the bare molecular Hamiltonian in the active space is replaced by a correlated effective Hamiltonian that incorporates dynamical correlation effects outside the active space. We benchmark our implementation on a linear \ce{H_6} chain, an \ce{H_6} lattice, an \ce{H_6} ring, and the \ce{N_2} molecule using the OpenFermion simulator. Our results show that operator elimination significantly reduces circuit depth and iteration count, and that OBDF-ADAPT-VQE yields energies closer to the full configuration interaction (FCI) reference than the standard approach within the same active space.
summary: The paper improves the ADAPT-VQE algorithm, which is used for quantum chemistry simulations, by implementing an operator elimination strategy that prunes redundant terms from the ansatz pool. Furthermore, they enhance accuracy by coupling this method with a One-Body Downfolding Framework (OBDF) to incorporate dynamic correlation effects into the active space Hamiltonian. This combination significantly reduces required quantum resources while achieving energies closer to exact reference values.
main_problem: The primary challenge is efficiently computing ground-state electronic structure energies for quantum chemistry and condensed matter systems, which suffer from the exponential scaling of exact methods like FCI.
main_result: The combination of operator elimination in ADAPT-VQE with One-Body Downfolding (OBDF) yields energy estimates significantly closer to high-accuracy reference methods than standard ADAPT-VQE within the same active space.
method: They propose an operator elimination scheme for ADAPT-VQE that removes non-contributing operators whose parameters vanish during optimization. This is combined with OBDF, which replaces the bare Hamiltonian in the active space with a correlated effective Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The work models molecular systems and materials using fermionic Hamiltonians. Benchmarking was performed on $\ce{H_6}$ chains, lattices, rings, and the $\ce{N_2}$ molecule, utilizing both Hartree-Fock (HF) and OBMP2 derived orbitals.
key_observables: Ground-state energy ($E_0$), circuit depth (CNOT gate counts), iteration count, and gradient norm convergence.
important_parameters: The elimination threshold ($\delta$) for vanishing parameters; the fraction of eliminated operators ($\phi$); and the active space definition derived from OBMP2.
main_assumptions: The permanent elimination scheme is preferred over pool restoration because restoration introduces optimization instabilities. The use of OBDF assumes that dynamic correlation effects outside the active space can be effectively captured by a one-body approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the workflow incorporating plateau-operator elimination into ADAPT-VQE, showing significant reductions in CNOT gate counts across $\ce{H_6}$ systems. Other figures compare energy convergence and Potential Energy Surfaces (PES) for various molecules ($\ce{N_2}$, $\ce{H_6}$) using different methods.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the limitations of standard VQE/ADAPT-VQE, then details the novel operator elimination technique to stabilize optimization and reduce circuit depth. Subsequently, it integrates this with the OBDF framework to incorporate external correlation effects, benchmarking performance across various molecular models.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource scaling in quantum simulation by providing a practical heuristic (operator elimination) to keep variational ansätze shallow while simultaneously improving accuracy via advanced embedding techniques (OBDF), making it highly relevant for near-term quantum hardware applications.
